problem: Zero-shot ObjectNav methods explore only a single floor, yet target objects often lie on other floors, so the agent fails even after fully exploring the current floor.
motivation: 57.3% of MP3D scenes contain target categories that are not confined to one floor, so single-floor exploration caps success. The paper adds an LLM-driven decision on when to climb stairs, plus stair traversal, on top of a zero-shot pipeline.
key_idea: Use an LLM plus hand-weighted exploration statistics (timestep, discovered object variety, recent explored-area gain) to decide when to leave the current floor via detected stairs, then traverse the stairs with a dedicated inter-floor navigation routine in a zero-shot semantic-map ObjectNav pipeline.
insight: Multi-floor reasoning helps because agents otherwise get stuck on a floor without the target. In the ablation (Table II), removing the explored-area term hurts most (SR 58.3 to 54.0, SPL 0.267 to 0.210), followed by timestep (55.8) and objects (56.2). Removing the LLM term costs less (57.1). The SPL gain is small because extra-floor exploration lengthens paths.
method: Semantic map + candidate waypoints: builds a top-down semantic map from RGB-D and GT pose (with a stair channel), derives frontier centroids, and scores them by benefit minus alpha*distance (as in PONI).

LLM-based policy: Qwen2 scores candidate points by the probability that the target co-occurs with the objects near them. Points with more than 90% explored area are skipped, and TriHelper's repeated-selection detection triggers free exploration.
VLM-based policy: Qwen2-VL-Int4 double-checks the current frame for the target. Its probability is fused with the Mask2Former segmentation confidence: C=beta*Pseg+(1-beta)*Pvlm.

Multi-floor Navigation Policy (MFNP): activated only when a stair is detected (Estair=1) and the timestep is between 150 and 300 (no climbing in the first 150 or last 200 steps). It computes N=w1*f(t)+w2*Oexplored/Ototal+w3*(1-Et)+w4*PLLM, with f(t)=(500-t)/500. The LLM is prompted with the timestep, objects and explored-area change. The agent goes up if N exceeds a threshold.

Inter-floor navigation: sets the stair area as the waypoint, dilates the stair entrance and marks it as an obstacle after entry to force one-way traversal, and resets the semantic map after 200 steps with MFNP temporarily disabled.
Navigation path policy: Fast Marching Method point-to-point planner produces the discrete actions.

setting.action_space: 6 discrete actions (forward, turn left/right, look up/down, stop) via waypoints from an FMM planner
setting.privileged: GT agent pose used for map building; the stair-climbing SDK on the real Unitree Go1 handles stair ascent

numbers.extra: success distance 0.1 m stated in text; 500-step budget
numbers.evidence: Table I: MFNP (Ours) HM3D SR 58.3, SPL 0.267, DTG 3.568
Table I: MFNP (Ours) MP3D SR 41.1, SPL 0.154, DTG 4.53

numbers_note: Table II caption says MP3D but the text says the ablation is on HM3D; the ALL-episode row (58.3/0.267/3.568) equals the HM3D Table I row. Splits are val (validation) and are not written as val-unseen in the paper.
results: MFNP reaches HM3D SR 58.3 / SPL 0.267 and MP3D SR 41.1 / SPL 0.154. It beats TriHelper (56.5 SR on HM3D) and VLFM (52.5 SR on HM3D; 36.4 on MP3D). On the multi-floor subset it beats TriHelper (38.5 vs 33.0 SR). SPL is lower than VLFM's (0.304 on HM3D, 0.175 on MP3D) because of longer paths. A real Unitree Go1 climbed stairs and found the target.
limitations: SPL is lower than the best baseline (VLFM) because of extra-floor exploration, and hand-tuned weights and thresholds are used
Only upward stair traversal is handled, with fixed timestep windows; real-world stair climbing relies on the robot's built-in SDK; only one qualitative real-world trial is shown
Relies on GT pose and on stair detection by the segmentation model
